_note: Covered regions. expected_trails is a collapse tripwire, self-baselined: the count this build measured on 13 Nov 2026; the build fails if a region comes in under 50% of it. It is not an independent OSM figure. classics: each name must be found in the region's names.json with a length in len_m (metres), be ranked first by the app's own name search, and have a stored gain within max_err_pct (default 15) of published_ft (one-way headline gain in feet, source given). stored_len_m: range for the stored (stitched) length when it differs from names.json. v1: also publish the frozen old-format copy at trails/ (Washington only). max_err_pct above 15 is a temporary allowance and only goes with a known_bug note; remove both when the stitcher is fixed.

classics.name: Dog Mountain Trails
classics.known_bug: known stitcher bug: chain starts away from the trailhead; remove when the stitcher is fixed
classics.detail: The stitched chain is 6.89 mi, the published loop length, but it dips to river level (the trailhead) mid-chain, adding a 1,128 ft up-and-down leg; trailhead to summit alone is 2,621 ft (-6.4%). Not DEM noise.

classics.name: Eagle Creek Trail
classics.note: Trailhead to Wahtum Lake: 1,500 ft over the first 7 miles plus 2,250 ft over the next 5, per that guide (sources vary).

classics.name: Misery Ridge
classics.note: Loop figure (5.09 mi, 700 ft); other guides give 910 to 1,100 ft for the ridge climb.

classics.name: Mist Trail
classics.note: Happy Isles to the top of Nevada Fall (the OSM relation ends there): 2.7 mi one way and 1,900 ft per that page, which cites the National Park Service. Gain to the top of Vernal Fall alone is about 1,000 ft.

classics.name: Matt Davis Trail
classics.note: Bay Area Ridge Trail guide: 6.4 mi one way for hikers, 770 ft gain and 730 ft loss. The Matt Davis route is also hiked as a 6.6 mi loop with Steep Ravine (about 1,700 ft, The Outbound), but OSM has no loop relation.

classics.name: Devils Backbone Trail
classics.note: Baldy Notch to the summit of Mount San Antonio: 3.3 mi and 2,350 ft one way, per that page. OSM spells it without the apostrophe.
